summary: Notes from a Data and File Transfer Workshop held at MIT on April 14 and 15, 1972, written by Abhay Bhushan. They summarize talks and the decisions reached, including ideas about a standard form for converting between different hosts' file formats. The goal was a data and file transfer approach that served big hosts, small hosts, TIPs and the Datacomputer.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 327 records workshop discussions and decisions about moving files between different computers. The participants agreed on design choices for control, data formats, transfer modes and recovery after failures.

questions: what did the data and file transfer workshop decide
subtitle: Workshop decisions on data and file transfer

tldr.problem: Different hosts had different ways to represent files, so a network transfer approach needed to preserve data and its meaning.
tldr.mechanism: Workshop participants agreed on separate control and data connections, printable commands, multiple representations and transfer modes, and a restart procedure.
tldr.outcome: The notes record decisions for a proposed file transfer protocol and assign work on a draft specification.

today: RFC 327 is a record of workshop decisions and discussion. It describes planned protocol design choices and says a draft specification would follow.

sections.title: The Workshop's Goal
sections.content:
The Data and File Transfer Workshop met at MIT on April 14 and 15, 1972. It aimed to develop a data and file transfer approach for the different kinds of ARPANET users and systems, including large and small hosts, TIPs, the Datacomputer, Remote Job Entry and mailbox users.

The goals included preserving the data, its character representation and, where practical, its structure. Participants did not agree on a general file-structure transformation scheme.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop sought transfer rules that could serve different computers and users. It wanted files to arrive with their data and character meanings intact.

sections.title: Separate Control and Data
sections.content:
The workshop decided to use one connection for control information and separate connections for the data. The control connection would use a full-duplex TELNET connection established through the Initial Connection Protocol. Data connections would be simplex connections established directly.

Commands and their arguments would be printable ASCII strings, so a person could use them at a terminal, while the interaction remained suitable for programs.
sections.plainLanguage: One connection would carry commands, and a separate connection would carry the file. Commands would use readable text rather than numeric codes.

sections.title: Data Representations and Transfer Modes
sections.content:
The notes list accepted representations including Network ASCII, Local Byte, Image, ASCII Print and EBCDIC Print. The workshop also defined transfer modes such as byte stream, block, ASCII, network ASCII with CR LF record endings, and HASP compressed files. Record structure could be used but was not mandatory.

Users could select the byte size, user socket, data representation and transfer mode through commands that received acknowledgments.
sections.plainLanguage: Files could be sent as text, raw image data or other listed forms. Users could also choose whether the transfer kept record boundaries or used a stream of bytes.

sections.title: Restarting After a Failure
sections.content:
The workshop agreed that a restart procedure should protect users from host or process failures. The sender would place markers in the data stream, and the receiver would record their corresponding positions. After a failure, the user could supply that information in a restart command to continue from a known point.

The notes assign Abhay Bhushan the task of writing workshop notes and a draft file transfer specification. They also decide that DTP would become transfer modes and format procedures within the file transfer protocol, rather than a separate protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: Markers in a transfer would let a user restart it from a recorded point after a system failure. The workshop also asked for a draft specification based on its decisions.
